verdict_reason: Amari's Fisher metric is the expectation of score outer products (and a natural gradient applies its inverse), while BLME returns the Euclidean squared norm of one observed-label score and computes neither object. For p=(0.9999,0.0001) and W=(0,1), the same predictive distribution yields 1e-8 or 0.99980001 depending on the observed label, whereas tr(F_h)=9.999e-5 with F_h=W^T(diag(p)-pp^T)W.
comparable_reason: The Euclidean hidden-coordinate norm is arbitrary across architectures: the exactly function-preserving change h'=c h, W'=W/c leaves all logits and probabilities fixed but divides the output by c^2. On Pythia-70M, c=2 preserved logits bit-for-bit and moved 0.3812 to 0.09531; across eight models the metric also tracked an unembedding-weight statistic with Pearson r=+0.976 and Spearman rho=+0.952.
github_reason: Fetched Amari's 1998 paper record and searched for author-released code; none was released for this theoretical work, and it contains no transformer hidden-state score-norm routine. The closed form itself was independently checked against float64 autograd and finite differences, but that verifies calculus, not provenance.
paper_reason: Amari reports Fisher-efficiency and learning behavior for parameter-space natural gradients, not ||grad_h log p(y|h)||^2 on language-model tokens. No published value exists for this BLME construction.
confounds_reason: A logit-identical c=2 reparameterization changes the metric by exactly 4x, proving a units/architecture confound without relying on observational correlation. Across eight models it correlates +0.976 with E_y||W_y-Wbar||^2; across four allowed models prior current-code measurements gave Spearman rho=+0.775 with d_model and -0.894 with vocab_size.
defects: CODE src/blme/tasks/geometry/information_geometry.py:108-120: the implementation samples the corpus label y and returns ||W_y-E_p[W]||^2. Fisher information requires E_{Y~p}[g_Y g_Y^T], whose trace is sum_k p_k||W_k||^2-||sum_k p_k W_k||^2; natural-gradient geometry additionally requires the Fisher metric/inverse.

CODE/SEMANTICS: the observed-label value is dominated by surprise as well as local distribution sensitivity; in the binary anchor it changes by 99,980,001x for common versus rare outcomes under exactly the same model distribution.
COMPARABILITY: h'=c h and W'=W/c preserves the represented function but rescales the result by 1/c^2, so the raw number has no architecture-independent units.

CODE information_geometry.py:98-107: _head_checked is set before validation. A failed nonlinear-head call marks the instance checked, so a second call skips the guard and emits a value from an invalid closed form.

CODE/DTYPE: the fixed relative-logit cutoff 1e-3 falsely rejects ordinary BF16 linear heads; measured deviations were 0.00246 (GPT-2), 0.00370 (Pythia-70M), and 0.00249 (Qwen2.5-0.5B), causing no feature output in seven of eight BF16 zoo runs.
CODE information_geometry.py:120-127: it averages token means within each document and then gives every document equal weight, so resegmenting an unchanged token stream changes the headline.
fix: Choose and name the estimand. For label-free Fisher sensitivity, compute F_h=W^T(diag(p)-pp^T)W or at least tr(F_h)=sum_k p_k||W_k||^2-||sum_k p_kW_k||^2; for a true natural-gradient quantity, use the Fisher metric/inverse. Emit an explicitly scale-invariant companion after validating its invariance, use the model's actual logits for post-head transforms, make the linear-head tolerance dtype-aware, set _head_checked only after success, and aggregate over tokens rather than document means.
